newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond and interest rate futures came under pressure on Friday as investors became more concerned about the possibility the ruling centre-right coalition might not win a majority in an upcoming parliamentary election.
June bond and PIBOR futures and PIBOR future started the day on a weak footing after the release of a poll late on Thursday which showed the coaltion would have only a slim majority.
During the day continued speculation that the left wing were edging ahead of the centre-right coalition hit the franc and interest rate futures although no fresh polls were released.

"There were rumours saying (polls show) a majority for the left and there was nervousness on this," the head of a French brokerage said. "We had support from cash early in the morning but its finished now."
He said one of the main concerns among traders was that the election could turn into a vote against Prime Minister Alain Juppe, who has a poor record in opinion polls.

The June bond future opened just above 128.20 support but managed to survive several tests and remained above 128 which traders said was a key technical level. It rallied as high as 128.40 just before the close but then drifted lower again.

One said besides general investor wariness about Europe as a whole, the belief the euro would still be launched but could be "softer" than many expect was also weighing on Bunds, allowing French 10-year bond yields to remain under Bund yields.

The franc fell as low as 3.3785 per mark as speculation about polls continued to weigh. The franc hit a high of 3.3685 on Thursday before the IPSOS poll was released. The franc climbed back to 3.3756 per mark late in the session as the German unit came under pressure against the dollar.
